subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` be a non-consuming operator verification action that never mutates scheduler-owned state, with only timer and gateway on-exit watcher paths allowed to consume one-shots?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility change to an existing public cron-run behavior and cannot be settled solely by tests or code structure.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Keep the proposed internal-origin design, provided current-head live proof confirms manual preservation and scheduler/watcher consumption without regressions.

options.title: Retain consuming manual runs
options.body: Reject the behavior change and pursue a narrower warning or explicit opt-in path if manual execution must continue consuming one-shots.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed internal-origin design, provided current-head live proof confirms manual preservation and scheduler/watcher consumption without regressions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged cron scheduling work establishes the due-slot and recomputation contracts most directly affected by this compatibility choice.
